correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md proof: the two fourth-order integer recurrence templates B_z(t), C_z(t) have characteristic polynomial (T^2-4T-1)(T^2+T-1) with unit constant term, so gcd over ANY integer tail equals gcd of four consecutive template values. Their four integer entries give 2 gcd(t-18,30) and 2 gcd(t+6,30); Fibonacci/Lucas triple-angle identities and exact telescoping express 20 S_F or 4 S_L in terms of these templates, with parity of m. Reducing the evaluated modular gcds by Fibonacci/Lucas periods modulo 2 and 3 yields the closed formula. The recurrence invertibility is essential: finite 4-shift GCD alone is not a proof absent that lemma. Independent integer arithmetic computed all ten consecutive window sums for m=1..100 in both sequences and found agreement; those checks corroborate but do not prove all m/n. Exact integer and divisibility boundaries m=1,2,3,4 were included.

value.rationale: Determines an entire infinite family of natural GCD invariants for Fibonacci/Lucas cubic translates, answering the cited precise higher-power problem. Nontrivial 2-, 3-, and 5-adic factors and parity transitions are not textbook first-power substitutions; the four-shift certificate makes it useful to future sequence arithmetic.

final_claim: For every integer m>=1, G_F(2m)=2^{-1_{3|m}}3^{1_{4|m}}(F_m if m even else L_m), and G_L(2m)=5^{1_{2|m}}G_F(2m), where G_X(k) is the gcd over all n>=0 of the k consecutive cubes X_{n+1}^3+...+X_{n+k}^3.
limitations: Only ordinary Fibonacci and Lucas sequences, positive even window lengths; no assertion for arbitrary generalized initial conditions or odd lengths.
Ten-shift checks do not certify the universal identity; proof is via recurrence templates.
